title: Auth Control Plane principal (v1 wire format)
description:
The resolved principal the Auth Control Plane hands to a relying party once a credential has been verified. Field-for-field this implements the canonical `principal.v1` document in TRD section 8, extended only where guardrail G-31 requires more than the TRD's example shows (see `grant_revision`/`entitlement_revision`).

This is a WIRE contract. The JSON Schema, the OpenAPI document that references it, and the golden fixtures under contracts/auth/v1/examples/principal/ are the source of truth; the Go, Python and TypeScript types are implementations of it, never the other way round (TRD section 2 principle 12, TRD section 21).

Distinct from contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.ops.json and credential-classes.json, which are the Wave 0 INVENTORY contract describing what authentication exists today. This file describes what the new service emits. Nothing here changes their semantics.

FOUR DELIBERATE OMISSIONS, all load-bearing, none an oversight to repair:
  * no `tier` and no `licensed_features` -- ACP-ADR-07 decision 2 makes entitlement an input to a DECISION and never a claim in a credential; G-14 forbids it by name; TRD section 8's own rule says "Grants and entitlements are not identity claims".
  * no `permissions` -- TRD section 11 and G-14 forbid embedding a complete mutable permission set in a credential. A relying party asks the authorization surface, which also binds entitlement (ACP-ADR-07 decision 3: both gates must pass independently).
  * no `role` -- ACP-ADR-05 decision 4 and G-27 require an explicit action at the call site and forbid a broad role check as the final decision.
  * no `is_superuser` -- TRD section 3 and G-23 move platform-admin authority to a separate platform role/action namespace resolved against CURRENT state. A superuser bit carried in a principal is the mechanism being migrated away from.
The existing effective-principal envelope (cmd/query-api/internal/principal/claims.go) carries all four today. It is the COMPATIBILITY implementation this migration retires; diffing this schema against that struct will show four things 'missing', and their absence is the decision.

schema_version.description: Identifies this document's contract. A relying party MUST reject an unrecognised value rather than parse optimistically (ACP-ADR-05 decision 1 / G-26: unknown denies). TRD section 21: contract evolution is additive within v1; breaking semantics require v2. Distinct from the three other version-shaped values in this system -- the effective-principal envelope's `v` claim, a principal's credential generation counter, and the `v1` path segment -- which move independently.

principal_id.description: Stable identifier for the acting principal, and THE AUTHORIZATION SUBJECT (TRD section 8 rule 1; G-20). Never an email, username, provider display name or token prefix, all of which are mutable. Opaque to relying parties: never parse it, never infer principal type from its shape.

principal_type.description: Which kind of principal is acting. This enum is REUSED VERBATIM from contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.schema.json ($defs.credentialClass.properties.principal_type), the Wave 0 closed vocabulary covering all 30 frozen credential classes, and matches TRD section 8's principal taxonomy. It is deliberately not a new vocabulary; a seventh kind is a change to that file first and this one second.

subject_id.description: The underlying subject record this principal resolves to -- a user id for a `human`, a service-account or workload record elsewhere. SEPARATE from principal_id by design (TRD section 8): the credential authenticates a principal but is not automatically the principal, and authorization keys on principal_id, never on this. null where the principal has no distinct underlying subject. A relying party that authorizes on subject_id has used the wrong field.

organization_id.description: Tenant this principal is acting within. null ONLY for a genuinely org-less principal (TRD section 8: "Organization may be absent for platform/pre-organization operations"). A relying party that scopes by organization MUST treat null as NO organization and DENY -- never as ANY organization. G-22: an organization is session context, not membership proof; membership is checked against authoritative state or an unexpired decision, never inferred from this field's presence.

credential.description: The credential that authenticated this principal. Present because TRD section 2 principle 1 makes credential class part of the route contract and G-2/G-3 forbid treating every bearer value as one class or discovering the class by validator fan-out. The credential authenticates a principal but IS NOT the principal (TRD section 8 rule 2).

class.description: Credential class, from the closed vocabulary. The first 30 values are the Wave 0 frozen set in contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.json; the remaining three are the new platform credentials TRD section 11 defines and which therefore cannot appear in a Wave 0 freeze of what exists today (`user_access_token`, `refresh_credential`, `workload_token`). Unknown denies (ACP-ADR-05 decision 1 / G-26). This enum is a DECLARATION, not a second source of truth: a guard test asserts it equals the ids in credential-classes.json plus exactly that documented addition list, so the two cannot drift and a new class cannot be smuggled in here alone.

credential_id.description: Opaque identifier for the credential instance (a session id, a registration id). An IDENTIFIER, never the secret: G-16 forbids a credential value in any fixture, log, trace, metric label or audit row, and G-17 makes plaintext secrets one-time output that list/read APIs never return.

issuer.description: Issuing authority. A verifier MUST pin an exact expected issuer (G-13). An empty expected issuer disables issuer checking outright in at least one widely used JWT library -- see NewVerifier's doc comment in cmd/query-api/internal/principal/verifier.go -- which fails OPEN, not closed.

audience.description: Exact intended audience (G-13, G-34: a token for one audience cannot call another). Same fail-open hazard as issuer when the expected value is empty.

scopes.description: Credential scopes, sorted. A DIFFERENT vocabulary from authorization actions: scopes bound what the credential may be used for, actions are what the authorization surface decides (G-5: authentication is not authorization). An empty array is a valid, meaningful value and MUST NOT be read as unrestricted.

items.description: A colon-separated scope such as `api:access` (TRD section 8). Deliberately a different shape from the dotted action names in an authorization decision, so the two vocabularies cannot be confused at a call site.

authentication.description: How and when this principal authenticated. `assurance` is a first-class input to authorization: G-31 names assurance as part of an allow-cache key and G-51 requires step-up gating for high-risk actions during impersonation, neither of which is expressible without it.

methods.description: Authentication methods used, sorted. Values are RFC 8176 `amr` names; this enum is the subset the platform's currently described flows can produce (TRD section 13: local password per the ACP-ADR-01 addendum, plus the MFA factors ACP-ADR-10 will settle). Unknown denies (G-26), so widening it is a deliberate schema amendment and ACP-ADR-10 is where MFA additions are decided. Federated sign-in is identified by the credential class and the upstream identity, not by an `amr` value.

authenticated_at.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the principal actually authenticated. NOT the same as `issued_at`: a principal document can be re-resolved many times from one authentication event, and a step-up decision needs the age of the AUTHENTICATION, not the age of this document. Written as an explicit [0-9] class and never \d: Python's `re` treats \d as UNICODE and accepts Devanagari and Arabic-Indic digits where Go RE2 and ECMA-262 treat it as ASCII -- MEASURED, and pinned by examples/principal/invalid-expires-at-unicode-digits.json. The `pattern` is the CROSS-LANGUAGE FLOOR: github.com/google/jsonschema-go records `format` and ignores it during validation (its doc.go, "Deviations from the specification"), so a constraint carried only by `format` is enforced in two languages out of three.

assurance.description: NIST SP 800-63B authenticator assurance level (TRD section 8 uses `aal1`). A relying party enforcing a step-up obligation compares against this; G-29 makes ignoring an obligation equivalent to ignoring a denial.

actor_chain.description:
Server-derived, append-only chain of delegation (TRD section 8 rule 4). EMPTY means the principal is acting as itself; the key is REQUIRED and the empty array explicit, so a deserializer defaulting a missing array to nil cannot make 'absent' read as 'not delegated'.

A chain rather than a single impersonator because G-49 requires the real actor and the effective subject BOTH to survive through token, decision, audit and downstream execution, and delegation can nest. The surrounding principal_id/subject_id/organization_id remain the EFFECTIVE (target) identity; the real actors appear only here. G-50: while delegated, permissions derive from the effective subject -- real-actor platform authority does not implicitly authorize target actions.

actor_principal_id.description: principal_id of the REAL actor acting as the effective subject.

delegation_id.description: Independent identifier for this delegated session, so it can be revoked on its own without revoking the base session (G-52).

reason.description: Why the delegation was granted. G-52 requires a reason to be recorded; it is an audit input, and G-65 forbids secrets or raw payloads in audit metadata.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 instant the delegated session began (G-52). Written as an explicit [0-9] class and never \d: Python's `re` treats \d as UNICODE and accepts Devanagari and Arabic-Indic digits where Go RE2 and ECMA-262 treat it as ASCII -- MEASURED, and pinned by examples/principal/invalid-expires-at-unicode-digits.json. The `pattern` is the CROSS-LANGUAGE FLOOR: github.com/google/jsonschema-go records `format` and ignores it during validation (its doc.go, "Deviations from the specification"), so a constraint carried only by `format` is enforced in two languages out of three.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry of THIS delegated session. ACP-ADR-03 sets it at 15 minutes and independently revocable, strictly shorter than the base session (G-52). It does not widen, and is not widened by, the enclosing principal's own expires_at: the effective deadline is the EARLIEST of all of them. Written as an explicit [0-9] class and never \d: Python's `re` treats \d as UNICODE and accepts Devanagari and Arabic-Indic digits where Go RE2 and ECMA-262 treat it as ASCII -- MEASURED, and pinned by examples/principal/invalid-expires-at-unicode-digits.json. The `pattern` is the CROSS-LANGUAGE FLOOR: github.com/google/jsonschema-go records `format` and ignores it during validation (its doc.go, "Deviations from the specification"), so a constraint carried only by `format` is enforced in two languages out of three.

permitted_actions.description: The bounded action set this delegation may exercise (G-52). Empty means the delegation authorizes no action by itself -- a valid, meaningful state, and never to be read as unrestricted.

items.description: A dotted, namespaced action such as `members.invite` or `acr.context.read` (ACP-ADR-05 decision 4). At least two segments is deliberate: a bare single segment is the shape of the `is_admin` check G-27 forbids, made unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

membership_revision.description:
Revision of the principal's organization memberships. Monotonic revision. ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 requires policy_revision in every decision, and G-31 requires an allow-cache key to bind principal, actor chain, credential/session, organization, action, resource, POLICY, MEMBERSHIP, GRANT and ENTITLEMENT revisions and assurance. A consumer caching anything derived from this principal MUST include all four in its cache key; a key built from a subset is a cache a revision bump cannot invalidate.

TRD section 8's example carries only membership_revision and policy_revision. That example is under-specified against G-31, which is stated as an acceptance criterion rather than a suggestion, so all four are carried here. Flat rather than nested to stay as close to the TRD's spelling as the guardrail allows.

policy_revision.description:
Revision of the active policy set. Monotonic revision. ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 requires policy_revision in every decision, and G-31 requires an allow-cache key to bind principal, actor chain, credential/session, organization, action, resource, POLICY, MEMBERSHIP, GRANT and ENTITLEMENT revisions and assurance. A consumer caching anything derived from this principal MUST include all four in its cache key; a key built from a subset is a cache a revision bump cannot invalidate.

TRD section 8's example carries only membership_revision and policy_revision. That example is under-specified against G-31, which is stated as an acceptance criterion rather than a suggestion, so all four are carried here. Flat rather than nested to stay as close to the TRD's spelling as the guardrail allows.

grant_revision.description:

ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 requires policy_revision in every decision, and G-31 requires an allow-cache key to bind principal, actor chain, credential/session, organization, action, resource, POLICY, MEMBERSHIP, GRANT and ENTITLEMENT revisions and assurance. entitlement_revision.description:
Revision of the entitlement projection this resolution saw. A CACHE-INVALIDATION input, not an entitlement value -- it says WHICH snapshot was current, never what it granted. Carrying the revision is what lets a consumer bind its cache correctly while the principal itself stays free of entitlement, which ACP-ADR-07 decision 2 requires. Monotonic revision. ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 requires policy_revision in every decision, and G-31 requires an allow-cache key to bind principal, actor chain, credential/session, organization, action, resource, POLICY, MEMBERSHIP, GRANT and ENTITLEMENT revisions and assurance. A consumer caching anything derived from this principal MUST include all four in its cache key; a key built from a subset is a cache a revision bump cannot invalidate.

TRD section 8's example carries only membership_revision and policy_revision. That example is under-specified against G-31, which is stated as an acceptance criterion rather than a suggestion, so all four are carried here. Flat rather than nested to stay as close to the TRD's spelling as the guardrail allows.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry of this principal document. ACP-ADR-03 removes the effective-principal envelope's per-call TTL override outright: a security bound any call site may widen is not a bound. Relying parties MUST enforce this and MUST NOT accept an issuer-supplied extension. Where an actor_chain entry expires sooner, THAT is the effective deadline.
